references.text: Godliness is fundamental to turning away from evil, just as the midwives feared God and refused to obey Pharaoh's wicked command.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, and the midwives' godliness led them to do what was right.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to obey the king's command because they feared God more than men, just as the midwives did.
Peter and the apostles declared that one must obey God rather than men, the same principle the midwives followed when they refused to kill the male infants.
Peter and John challenged the religious leaders about whether it was right to obey them instead of God, the same dilemma the midwives faced.
Joseph said he feared God, the same godliness that motivated the midwives to act justly.
The command to fear God is repeated in the Torah and underlies the midwives' actions.
Moses' parents hid him in faith and did not fear the king's command, consistent with the midwives' godliness and disobedience to Pharaoh.
